title: Protest in Prague against broadcasting fees and for Czech TV reform

tea.why: Protesters oppose the current funding model of public media and demand reforms to Czech Television and Czech Radio.
tea.want: Abolition of mandatory broadcasting fees and structural reform of public media institutions.
tea.changed: Nov 7: Protesters marched to the Czech Television building in Prague to demand the abolition of broadcasting fees.

summary: On November 7, 2026, a protest organised by the Svatopluk association took place in Prague. Participants marched from the Congress Centre to the Czech Television building to demand the abolition of mandatory broadcasting fees and reforms to public media institutions. The event featured speeches from various public figures, including politician Kateřina Konečná and actor Oldřich Kaiser. A small group of counter-protesters also gathered at the site, leading to minor noise disturbances, but police reported the event concluded without significant issues. The protest follows ongoing national debates regarding a government proposal to shift public media funding to the state budget, a move critics argue threatens media independence. Authorities monitored the gathering with dozens of police officers present.
response: Police spokesperson Jan Rybanský stated that one individual was reported to authorities for disruptive behavior during the protest.

crowd.text: Organisers claimed 2,000 participants, while a news agency correspondent estimated several hundred.

updates.text: Protesters marched to the Czech Television building in Prague to demand the abolition of broadcasting fees.
